title: Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya — Heart of Recognition
author: Kṣemarāja
text:
The Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya — the 'Heart of Recognition' — is Kṣemarāja's five-verse summary of the recognition doctrine, the most influential compact manual to emerge from tenth-century Kashmir. Its opening question sets the entire problem: how does free consciousness, unborrowing and self-luminous, become the bound knower it seems to be? The five verses answer in order — the cause and its play, the structure of bondage, the special knowledge that reverses it, and the recognition itself, by which the self re-cognizes what it never ceased to be.

Its juice: 'Heart' means quintessence: this is the whole of Utpaladeva's vast system carried in five verses, meant to be memorized and lived with. Its juice is economy of the highest order — a complete metaphysics that can be recited before breakfast and still withhold nothing.
